components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tiàowǔ.
example.english: She likes dancing.
example.fact: 舞 is a verb and noun, but in modern speech it nearly always appears with 跳 in 跳舞 ('to dance'). Common compounds include 舞会 (ball, dance party) and 芭蕾舞 (ballet).

examples.pinyin: Tā zài tái shang tiàowǔ.
examples.english: She is dancing on stage.

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang xuéxiào yǒu wǔhuì.
examples.english: There is a dance at school tonight.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.pinyin: Kànlai tā jīntiān bú huì lái le.
example.english: It looks like he won't be coming today.
example.fact: 看来 almost always opens a sentence as a stand-alone adverb, signaling the speaker's own inference from visible evidence ("from how it looks...") — distinct from 好像 ("it seems, as if"), which can sit mid-sentence and does not necessarily imply the speaker reasoned it out from something observed.

examples.pinyin: Kànlai jīntiān yào jiābān le.
examples.english: It seems we'll work overtime today.

examples.pinyin: Tā kànlai hěn lèi.
examples.english: He looks tired.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.

example.pinyin: Tā gèzi hěn gāo.
example.english: He is very tall.
example.fact: 高 covers 'tall' for people and buildings, 'high' for levels and prices, and is also a common surname. Its opposite is 矮 (ǎi, short) for people but 低 (dī, low) for levels.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò dàlóu yǒu duō gāo?
examples.english: How tall is this building?

examples.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé tài gāo le.
examples.english: This price is too high.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — a building, as in 店, 床, 度: hemp stalks drying in a shed. 麻 also gives sound to 磨 mó, 摩 mó and 魔 mó.
火 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn, 热 hot: a hot, fevered head, hence vexed.
页 (head) is a loose sound clue for fán; as a meaning part 页 means head or page.

example.pinyin: Máfan nǐ bāng wǒ kāi yíxià mén.
example.english: Could you please help me open the door?
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense "trouble, hassle," 麻烦 doubles as one of Mandarin's most common polite openers for a request — 麻烦你... ("sorry to trouble you, but...") softens an imposition the same way English "sorry to bother you" does before asking a favor.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng tài máfan nǐ le.
examples.english: This is too much trouble for you.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yùdàole yí ge xiǎo máfan.
examples.english: I ran into a small problem.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 天上突然出现了一道彩虹。
example.pinyin: Tiānshàng tūrán chūxiàn le yí dào cǎihóng.
example.english: A rainbow suddenly appeared in the sky.
example.fact: 出现 describes something coming into view or into existence for the first time (出现问题 "a problem arises") — its cousin 表现 (also in this batch) instead describes how something behaves once it is already there, a distinction easy to blur since both share the character 现.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú chūxiàn le.
examples.english: He finally showed up.

examples.hanzi: 最近街上出现了很多新店。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn jiē shàng chūxiànle hěn duō xīn diàn.
examples.english: Lots of new shops have appeared on the street recently.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shǔjià dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
example.english: What do you plan to do for summer vacation?
example.fact: 打算 signals a fairly loose, still-flexible intention ("what I'm thinking of doing"), a notch less firm than 计划 ("plan"), which implies something more deliberately mapped out — asking 你打算做什么 sounds more casual than asking 你有什么计划.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn míngnián qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: I plan to go to China next year.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme dǎsuàn?
examples.english: What are your plans?

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
example.english: Let's go watch a movie this weekend.
example.fact: 电影 literally means "electric shadow" (电 "electricity" + 影 "shadow, image") — coined when film was a genuinely new technology, the same "electric ___" pattern that produced 电话 ("electric speech," telephone) and 电脑 ("electric brain," computer).

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: This movie is very good.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànyǐngyuàn ménkǒu děng nǐ.
examples.english: He's waiting for you at the entrance of the cinema.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ shì yi shì.
example.english: You can give it a try.
example.fact: 试 is often doubled or followed by 一下 for a soft suggestion: 试试 or 试一下. It is the verb for trying on clothes (试衣服) and appears in 考试 (exam) and 试用 (trial use).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ shìchuān zhè jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: You can try on this dress.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ yǒu yí ge kǎoshì.
examples.english: There is an exam tomorrow morning.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shēnshang yǒu méiyǒu dài qián?
example.english: Do you have any money on you?
example.fact: 身上 literally means "on the body," but its most common everyday use asks whether someone is carrying something on their person right now (身上有钱吗 "do you have money on you") — functionally closer to English "on me/on you" than to any literal reference to skin or clothing.

examples.pinyin: Tā shēnshang dōu shì hàn.
examples.english: He's covered in sweat.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshang méiyǒu dài shǒujī.
examples.english: I don't have my phone on me.

components.note: 户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ fángjiān dǎsǎo yíxià.
example.english: Please clean up the room a bit.
example.fact: 房间 names a single enclosed room within a larger building (一个房间 "a room") — for the building or dwelling as a whole, Chinese instead uses 房子 (also in this batch), a whole/part distinction that English blurs by using "room" loosely for both in casual speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān zài èr lóu.
examples.english: My room is on the second floor.

examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān yǒu liǎng zhāng chuáng.
examples.english: This room has two beds.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měi.
example.english: The scenery here is very beautiful.
example.fact: 美 is also the short name for America (美国) in Chinese, and it forms 美丽, 美味 (delicious), 美好 (wonderful). It is a more literary or formal word for 'beautiful' than 漂亮, which is typical for describing people.

examples.pinyin: Tā chànggē de shēngyīn hěn měi.
examples.english: Her singing voice is beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de yèjǐng zhēn měi!
examples.english: This city's night view is really beautiful!

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 不管天气怎么样,我们都会去。
example.pinyin: Bùguǎn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, wǒmen dōu huì qù.
example.english: No matter what the weather is like, we'll go.
example.fact: 不管 sets up a "no matter what" clause that is regularly completed later in the sentence by 都 ("in every case") — the same "no matter...都..." skeleton that 无论 also uses, making 不管 one half of a fixed two-part frame rather than a word that stands alone.

examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn duō wǎn, wǒ dōu děng nǐ.
examples.english: No matter how late, I'll wait for you.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù guǎn biérén zěnme shuō.
examples.english: He doesn't care what other people say.

components.note: 书 (simplified 書) — the old form shows a brush 聿 writing; to write, then what is written: book, letter.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile yì běn shū.
example.english: I bought a book.
example.fact: 书 takes the measure word 本 (一本书). It also appears in 书包 (school bag), 书店 (bookstore), 图书馆 (library) and in 读书, which can mean either 'to read' or 'to study'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài túshūguǎn kàn shū.
examples.english: I like reading in the library.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu sān běn shū.
examples.english: There are three books on the table.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.pinyin: Zhège dìfang tèbié ānjìng.
example.english: This place is especially quiet.
example.fact: 特别 works two ways: as an adjective meaning "special, unusual" describing a noun (特别的礼物 "a special gift"), and as an intensifying adverb before another adjective meaning "especially" (特别安静 "especially quiet") — the same word doing two different jobs depending on where it sits.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tèbié xǐhuan zhè shǒu gē.
examples.english: I especially like this song.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì ge tèbié de rìzi.
examples.english: Today is a special day.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 过马路的时候要注意安全。
example.pinyin: Guò mǎlù de shíhou yào zhùyì ānquán.
example.english: When crossing the road, pay attention to safety.
example.fact: 注 by itself means "to pour, to direct toward," as water is directed into a vessel, and 意 means "mind, intention" — 注意 pictures directing one's mind toward something, the same "directed attention" image behind the English idiom "pay attention."

examples.pinyin: Shàngkè yào zhùyì tīngjiǎng.
examples.english: Pay attention in class.

examples.hanzi: 大家请注意,火车马上进站。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā qǐng zhùyì, huǒchē mǎshàng jìnzhàn.
examples.english: Attention everyone, the train is about to arrive.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.pinyin: Tā zài tī qiú.
example.english: He is kicking a ball.
example.fact: 球 is both a ball and a sport in compound words such as 足球 (football/soccer), 篮球 (basketball) and 地球 (the Earth). The verb pairs with the sport: 踢球 (kick), 打球 (hit or play), 投球 (throw).

examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài cāochǎng shang tī qiú.
examples.english: The kids are playing soccer on the field.

examples.pinyin: Qiú diàojìn hé lǐ le.
examples.english: The ball fell into the river.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.

example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ chá yíxià dìtú.
example.english: Please check the map.
example.fact: 查 covers checking and looking something up: 查字典 (look up in a dictionary), 查电话 (look up a number) and 检查 (inspect). In 调查 (to survey) it means to investigate, and the surname Zhā uses the same character with a different reading.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chá yíxià zhège zì.
examples.english: I'd like to look up this character.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yào gěi tā zuò jiǎnchá.
examples.english: The doctor will give him a check-up.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thinking: 想 think, 思, 感 feel, 忙; forgetting is a loss of the heart's hold.
亡 (wáng, lose) gives the sound and fits the sense: to lose from the mind.

example.pinyin: Bié wàng le dài sǎn.
example.english: Don't forget to bring an umbrella.
example.fact: 忘 is often paired with 了 to make 忘了 ('forgot'), and 别忘了 is the common way to say 'don't forget to'. It also appears in the set phrase 忘记 and in 难忘 ('unforgettable').

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàngle tā de míngzi.
examples.english: I forgot his name.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ qiānwàn búyào wàng.
examples.english: Whatever you do, don't forget this.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — sweet taste, as in 甜: 甚 first meant great enjoyment, then "very, extremely".
至 (arrive) — oldest form is an arrow landing on a mark: to reach. 至 sounds out 到 dào and 致 zhì, and sits in 室 shì room and 屋 wū.

example.hanzi: 他忙得甚至没有时间吃饭。
example.pinyin: Tā máng de shènzhì méiyǒu shíjiān chīfàn.
example.english: He's so busy he doesn't even have time to eat.
example.fact: 甚至 pushes a statement to its most extreme, surprising case ("even...") and often pairs with 都 or 也 later in the sentence for emphasis — it leans more formal than the everyday 连...都... construction, which does very similar work in casual speech.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, shènzhì bù xiǎng shuōhuà.
examples.english: He's tired and doesn't even want to talk.

examples.hanzi: 他甚至不知道我的名字。
examples.pinyin: Tā shènzhì bù zhīdào wǒ de míngzi.
examples.english: He doesn't even know my name.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi bǎohù huánjìng.
example.english: We should protect the environment.
example.fact: 保护 protects something from harm before it happens — the environment, one's eyes, a species — while 保证 (also in this batch, sharing the character 保) instead guarantees an outcome or promise; both build on 保's core sense of "to look after," just applied to physical safety versus a spoken assurance.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù yǎnjing.
examples.english: We should protect our eyes.

examples.hanzi: 小狗受到了很好的保护。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu shòudàole hěn hǎo de bǎohù.
examples.english: The puppy was well protected.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.pinyin: Tā cái shì zhēnzhèng de péngyou.
example.english: He is a true friend.
example.fact: 真 and 正 are near-synonyms on their own — 真 means "real, true" and 正 means "correct, upright" — 真正 reinforces the two into one emphatic word, the same doubling-up strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 from the pilot batch, just with a different pair of near-synonyms.

examples.pinyin: Zhè cái shì zhēnzhèng de Zhōngguó cài.
examples.english: This is real Chinese food.

examples.pinyin: Zhēnzhèng de péngyou bú huì piàn nǐ.
examples.english: A true friend won't deceive you.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.pinyin: Kǎoshì jiéguǒ míngtiān gōngbù.
example.english: The exam results will be announced tomorrow.
example.fact: 结果 has two distinct readings that CEDICT sources can blur: read jiéguǒ (结 in its common jié tone, "to tie, to form"), it means "result, outcome" and is one of the most frequent nouns in Mandarin — while read jiēguǒ (结 in the rarer jiē tone), it instead means literally "to bear fruit," describing a plant. The high-frequency word behind this entry is the jiéguǒ "outcome" sense, not the far rarer horticultural jiēguǒ.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de nǔlì yǒule hǎo jiéguǒ.
examples.english: Your efforts paid off with a good result.

examples.pinyin: Jiéguǒ tā méi lái.
examples.english: As it turned out, he didn't come.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中表现得很好。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng biǎoxiàn de hěn hǎo.
example.english: He performed very well in the competition.
example.fact: 表现 works as a verb ("to perform, to behave") and a noun ("performance") without changing form — 表现得很好 uses it as a verb followed by a manner complement, while 他的表现很好 uses the exact same word as the subject noun of the sentence.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī biǎoyángle tā de biǎoxiàn.
examples.english: The teacher praised his performance.

examples.hanzi: 她在会上表现得很自信。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huì shàng biǎoxiàn de hěn zìxìn.
examples.english: She came across as very confident at the meeting.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 拍 is clapping or patting with the hand, also used for filming and taking photos.
白 (bái) — loose hint — 拍 is pāi; 白 also sounds out 伯 bó and 怕 pà.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒmen pāi zhāng zhào.
example.english: Please take a photo of us.
example.fact: 拍 literally means to pat or clap with a flat hand (拍手, to clap), but it is now the verb for taking photos (拍照) and for filming (拍电影). It also forms 拍卖 (auction) and 球拍 (racket).

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan pāi zhàopiàn.
examples.english: He likes taking photos.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ pāishǒu huānyíng tā.
examples.english: Everyone clapped to welcome him.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qíshí bú tài xǐhuan kāfēi.
example.english: Actually, I don't really like coffee.
example.fact: 其实 typically introduces a mild correction or a truth that contradicts what was just said or assumed ("actually, the truth is...") — a common way to soften disagreement or a surprising admission without directly contradicting the other person outright.

examples.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ yě bù zhīdào.
examples.english: Actually, I don't know either.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很凶,其实人很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlai hěn xiōng, qíshí rén hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He looks fierce, but he's actually very nice.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, dìshang hěn huá!
example.english: Be careful, the floor is slippery!
example.fact: 小 means "small" and 心 means "heart, mind" — 小心 literally pictures keeping one's mind small and tightly focused on a task, rather than "small-hearted" in the English sense of stingy or cowardly; the compositional logic runs the opposite direction from what an English speaker might guess.

examples.pinyin: Guò mǎlù yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Be careful crossing the road.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎoxīn bié shuāidǎo le.
examples.english: Be careful not to fall.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.pinyin: Qǐng jìnlái zuò yíhuìr.
example.english: Please come in and sit for a while.
example.fact: 进来 pairs 进 ("to enter") with 来 ("toward the speaker"), said by someone already inside inviting someone in. Swapping in 去 instead gives 进去 (also in this batch), reversing the viewpoint to "entering, away from the speaker" — the same 来/去 contrast found in 回来/回去 and 下来/下去.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn lěng, kuài jìnlái ba.
examples.english: It's cold outside, come on in.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng ménkǒu zǒu jìnlái le.
examples.english: He walked in through the door.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn cháng.
example.english: This road is very long.
example.fact: 路 uses the measure word 条 (一条路) and extends to routes and ways: 路线 (route), 路上 (on the way), 一路平安 (have a safe trip), and bus numbers (3路). 路 can also be an abstract path or method, as in 出路 (way out).

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù tōngxiàng huǒchēzhàn ma?
examples.english: Does this road lead to the train station?

examples.hanzi: 路上小心，到家给我打电话。
examples.pinyin: Lùshang xiǎoxīn, dào jiā gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Be careful on the way, and call me when you get home.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a mouth 口 on a tree 木: standing stiff and blank like a tree; 呆 means dull or to stay put, as in 发呆.

example.pinyin: Bié fādāi le, kuài zuò zuòyè ba.
example.english: Stop spacing out and do your homework.
example.fact: 呆 appears mostly in 发呆 (to stare blankly, zone out) and 呆板 (stiff, wooden). In the sense 'to stay' it is read dāi and is also written 待 in the north (呆在家里, 'stay at home'); 书呆子 is a bookworm.

examples.pinyin: Tā dāidāi de kànzhe chuāngwài.
examples.english: He stared blankly out the window.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng zài jiā dāizhe.
examples.english: I want to stay at home this weekend.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
example.english: There are four people in my family.
example.fact: 四 sounds close to 死 (sǐ, death), so many Chinese people avoid it in phone numbers, floor numbers and gifts. In Chinese buildings the fourth floor is often skipped, similar to the 13th floor in the West.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sì diǎn yí kè.
examples.english: It's a quarter past four.

examples.hanzi: 我们四个人一起去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen sì ge rén yìqǐ qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: The four of us are going on a trip together.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.

example.pinyin: Wǒ děngle hěn jiǔ.
example.english: I waited a long time.
example.fact: 久 describes how long something lasts, usually after 很 or in 好久 ('a very long time'). It is also in the greeting 好久不见 ('long time no see') and in 久违, a more formal way to greet someone you have not seen for a while.

examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, nǐ hǎo ma?
examples.english: Long time no see, how are you?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ děngle duōjiǔ?
examples.english: How long have you been waiting?

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 我当时并不知道发生了什么。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dāngshí bìng bù zhīdào fāshēng le shénme.
example.english: At the time, I really didn't know what had happened.
example.fact: 当时 always points back to a specific past moment already established in the conversation ("at that time, back then") — unlike 现在 ("now," from the pilot batch), which anchors to the moment of speaking, 当时 can never refer to the present.

examples.pinyin: Dāngshí wǒ cái shí suì.
examples.english: I was only ten at the time.

examples.pinyin: Dāngshí de tiānqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The weather was lovely at that time.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon guarding a place 口: 或 first meant a defended territory (域 yù adds 土). "Perhaps, or" is a later use.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá huò kāfēi?
example.english: Would you like tea or coffee?
example.fact: 或 and 还是 both mean 'or', but 或 is used in statements (茶或咖啡都可以) while 还是 is used in questions (茶还是咖啡？). 或 also appears in 或者 (or) and 或许 (perhaps).

examples.pinyin: Zhōuliù huò zhōurì wǒ dōu yǒu kòng.
examples.english: I'm free on Saturday or Sunday.

examples.hanzi: 你可以发邮件或打电话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ fā yóujiàn huò dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: You can send an email or call.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 情, 快, 忙; 懂 is to understand.
董 (dǒng) gives the sound exactly: 懂 dǒng.

example.pinyin: Nǐ dǒng wǒ de yìsi ma?
example.english: Do you understand what I mean?
example.fact: 懂 is often used with 不 or 得 as a complement: 听不懂 (can't understand by listening), 看懂了 (understood by reading). It is stronger than 知道 (to know a fact) and means to really grasp something.

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì wǒ bú tài dǒng.
examples.english: I don't quite get this character.

examples.hanzi: 他很懂事，大家都喜欢他。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn dǒngshì, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: He is sensible, and everyone likes him.

meanings: (used to express lack of alternatives) can only

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǐyǒu yí gè mèimei.
example.english: He only has one younger sister.
example.fact: 只有 frequently sets up a "the only way is..." clause completed later by 才 ("only then"), as in 只有努力才能成功 ("only through hard work can one succeed") — a fixed two-part frame parallel to 不管...都... elsewhere in this batch, where a first half sets a condition and a later adverb locks it in.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zhǐyǒu yì jiā shāngdiàn.
examples.english: There's only one shop here.

examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu nǔlì, cái néng chénggōng.
examples.english: Only by working hard can you succeed.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.

example.hanzi: 如果他不同意,我们怎么办?
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ tā bù tóngyì, wǒmen zěnmebàn?
example.english: If he doesn't agree, what should we do?
example.fact: Built from 怎么 ("how," pilot batch) plus 办 ("to handle"), 怎么办 literally asks "how to handle it" — but it is just as often blurted out completely alone, as a one-word cry of "What do I do?!", functioning as a stand-alone exclamation of panic as much as a real question.

examples.pinyin: Yàoshi diū le zěnmebàn?
examples.english: What should I do if I lose my keys?

examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu shíjiān le, zěnmebàn?
examples.english: We're out of time, what do we do?

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dì yī cì lái zhèlǐ.
example.english: This is my first time here.
example.fact: 第 is placed before a number to make it ordinal: 第一 (first), 第二天 (the second day). Unlike English, you put 第 directly before the number and then a measure word: 第三个 (the third one).

examples.pinyin: Dì yī tiān shàngbān, wǒ hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: On my first day at work, I was nervous.

examples.pinyin: Tā kǎole quán bān dì sān míng.
examples.english: He ranked third in the whole class.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.pinyin: Nà pǐ mǎ pǎo de hěn kuài.
example.english: That horse runs very fast.
example.fact: 马 takes the measure word 匹. Horses appear in many idioms: 马上 (immediately, 'on horseback'), 马马虎虎 (so-so) and 一马当先 (take the lead). It is also a very common surname and in names like 马来西亚.

examples.pinyin: Cǎodì shang yǒu yì pǐ báimǎ.
examples.english: There is a white horse on the grass.

examples.pinyin: Háizimen hěn xiǎng qí mǎ.
examples.english: The children really want to ride a horse.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài jiǎng gùshi.
example.english: The teacher is telling a story.
example.fact: 讲 is more formal and deliberate than 说: it fits lectures, stories and explanations (讲课, 讲道理). It also means 'to be particular about', as in 讲卫生 (to care about hygiene) and 讲究.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jiǎng de màn yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Please speak a bit slower.

examples.hanzi: 老师给我们讲了一个故事。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen jiǎngle yí ge gùshi.
examples.english: The teacher told us a story.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 给, 经: cutting a thread, hence to break off.
色 (sè) is only a loose sound clue for jué.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.pinyin: Zhè juéduì shì gè hǎo zhǔyi.
example.english: This is absolutely a good idea.
example.fact: 绝 alone means "to cut off completely, to sever" — the same "cutting off" sense shows up in 拒绝 ("to refuse," literally "to sever/resist") — an image of severing all alternatives that gives 绝对 its sense of "no exceptions, no room for doubt."

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài juéduì hǎochī.
examples.english: This dish is absolutely delicious.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéduì bú huì gàosu biérén.
examples.english: I'll absolutely never tell anyone.

meanings: sir (term of address for senior officer)

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.pinyin: “Shì, zhǎngguān!” shìbīng dàshēng huídá.
example.english: "Yes, sir!" the soldier replied loudly.
example.fact: 长 is one of Mandarin's most common heteronyms: read zhǎng (as here) it means "chief, head, elder" (长官 "commanding officer," also 校长 "principal"); read cháng it instead means "long" in length or duration (长城 "the Great Wall") — one character splitting into two unrelated meanings depending on tone.

examples.pinyin: Zhǎngguān, qǐngwèn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Officer, excuse me, how do I get there?

examples.pinyin: Zhǎngguān ràng dàjiā zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
examples.english: The commander told everyone to rest early.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de yuángōng.
example.english: He is an employee of our company.
example.fact: 员 is a bound form used as a suffix for people with a role: 演员 (actor), 服务员 (waiter), 运动员 (athlete), 公务员 (civil servant). It is almost never used alone.

examples.hanzi: 这个饭店的服务员很热情。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fàndiàn de fúwùyuán hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: The waiters at this restaurant are very friendly.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge shì gōngsī zhíyuán.
examples.english: My older brother is a company employee.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 他敲了敲门,然后走了进去。
example.pinyin: Tā qiāo le qiāo mén, ránhòu zǒu le jìnqù.
example.english: He knocked on the door, then walked in.
example.fact: 进去 completes 进 ("to enter") with 去 ("away from the speaker") instead of 来 — said from the perspective of someone outside, or narrating someone else moving further inside, the mirror image of 进来 earlier in this batch.

examples.pinyin: Háizi pǎo jìnqu le.
examples.english: The child ran inside.

examples.hanzi: 外面太冷了,我们进去吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, wǒmen jìnqu ba.
examples.english: It's too cold outside, let's go in.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — oldest form is an arrow landing on a mark: to reach. 至 sounds out 到 dào and 致 zhì, and sits in 室 shì room and 屋 wū.
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zhìshǎo yīnggāi shuō shēng xièxie.
example.english: You should at least say thank you.
example.fact: 至 means "to arrive, to reach a limit" and 少 means "few, little" — 至少 literally pictures "reaching down to the smallest amount," the lower bound of what's acceptable, a logic mirrored by its opposite 至多 ("at most," reaching up to the largest amount).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhìshǎo yào shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I need to sleep at least seven hours.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu zhìshǎo wǔbǎi kuài.
examples.english: This piece of clothing costs at least five hundred yuan.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking and conduct, as in 行, 往, 得, 很.
聿 (brush) — writing the rules: 律 is law, and a rule of rhythm.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 她请了一位律师帮她打官司。
example.pinyin: Tā qǐng le yí wèi lǜshī bāng tā dǎ guānsi.
example.english: She hired a lawyer to help her with her lawsuit.
example.fact: 律师 takes the respectful measure word 位 rather than the neutral 个 (一位律师, not 一个律师) — the same polite 位 used for teachers and doctors, a small measure-word choice that signals respect for the profession.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge shì yì míng lǜshī.
examples.english: My older brother is a lawyer.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào zhǎo lǜshī bāngmáng.
examples.english: You need to find a lawyer to help.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.pinyin: Tā zhěnggè xiàwǔ dōu zài shuìjiào.
example.english: He slept the whole afternoon.
example.fact: 整个 always sits directly before a noun as a modifier (整个下午 "the whole afternoon", 整个城市 "the whole city") and cannot stand alone as a full predicate the way 所有 (pilot batch) sometimes can — the two "whole/all" words divide the grammatical labor of English "whole" and "all" between them.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhěnggè zhōumò dōu zài jiā.
examples.english: I was at home the whole weekend.

examples.hanzi: 整个城市都安静下来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhěnggè chéngshì dōu ānjìng xiàlai le.
examples.english: The whole city became quiet.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdào yǒu rén zài qiāo mén.
example.english: I heard someone knocking on the door.
example.fact: 到 acts as a resultative complement meaning "successfully reaching a target" — 听到 literally means "listen and successfully arrive at [the sound]," i.e. actually hearing it, in contrast to the plain verb 听 ("to listen"), which just describes the act without confirming anything registered. The same 到-as-"successfully" pattern shows up in 看到 ("to see," lit. "look and reach") and 找到 ("to find," lit. "search and reach").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīngdào nǐ shuō shénme.
examples.english: I didn't hear what you said.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tīngdào nàge shēngyīn le ma?
examples.english: Did you hear that sound?

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在台上表演节目。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài tái shàng biǎoyǎn jiémù.
example.english: The children are performing on stage.
example.fact: 表演 covers both scripted, rehearsed performance (a play, a dance routine, a magic show) and, by extension, "putting on an act" insincerely in everyday speech (别表演了, "stop putting on a show") — the same slide from "staged performance" to "fake behavior" that English "act" undergoes.

examples.pinyin: Tā de wǔdǎo biǎoyǎn hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: Her dance performance was wonderful.

examples.hanzi: 明天晚上学校有音乐表演。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǎnshang xuéxiào yǒu yīnyuè biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: There's a music performance at school tomorrow night.

meanings: to be in the process of

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài xiě zuòyè.
example.english: He is in the middle of doing his homework.
example.fact: 正在 is one of Mandarin’s clearest markers of the progressive aspect ("right now, in the middle of") and sits directly before the verb — it is often reinforced by the sentence-final particle 呢 (他正在写作业呢), but unlike English "-ing," it can be dropped entirely once context already makes an ongoing action obvious.

examples.hanzi: 我正在开车,晚点打给你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài kāichē, wǎndiǎn dǎ gěi nǐ.
examples.english: I'm driving, I'll call you back later.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn zhèngzài xià dàyǔ.
examples.english: It's pouring outside right now.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.

example.pinyin: Tā wú jiā kě guī.
example.english: He has no home to return to.
example.fact: 无 is a literary 'no' or 'without', as in 无法 (unable to), 无聊 (boring), 无论 (no matter) and the idiom 无家可归. It is the simplified form of 無, and it corresponds to colloquial 没有 and 不.

examples.hanzi: 你无法一个人完成这件事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wúfǎ yí ge rén wánchéng zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: You can't finish this alone.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí wúguān jǐnyào.
examples.english: This question is of no importance.
